old: The translative case suffix *-vá / -vé* denotes changing or turning into something (*otthonná alakít* = convert into a home; *szebbé tesz* = make prettier). If the noun ends in a consonant, the *v* assimilates to that consonant: *ház + -vá = házzá*, *lakás + -vá = lakássá*, *kert + -vé = kertté*.
new: You know the translative *-vá / -vé* from A2 Unit 35: it says what something becomes or is turned into (*otthonná* = into a home, *szebbé* = into prettier). After a consonant the *v* turns into that consonant: *ház + -vá = házzá*, *lakás + -vá = lakássá*, *kert + -vé = kertté*. Here you use it for home projects.
why: recap, not new (A2 Unit 35); *otthonná alakít* used unmet alakít

old: Notice the pair: *valami válik valamivé* (intransitive: something becomes something, e.g., *a ház otthonná válik*), while *valaki tesz valamit valamivé* (transitive: someone makes/turns something into something, e.g., *a növények otthonossá teszik a szobát*).
new: You know *válik* (becomes) and *tesz* (makes) with *-vá / -vé* from A2 Unit 35. *Valami válik valamivé*: no object, it changes by itself (*a szoba világossá válik*). *Valaki tesz valamit valamivé*: someone makes something into something (*a lámpa világossá teszi a szobát*).

old: Rental contracts (*bérleti szerződés*) use legal expressions: *köteles* (+ infinitive: is obliged to), *jogosult* (+ infinitive / *-ra*: is entitled to), and *esetén* (+ noun: in case of, e.g., *késedelem esetén* = in case of delay).
new: You know *kell* and *muszáj* + infinitive from A1 Unit 24. Formal texts and contracts also use *köteles* (is obliged to: a rule or a contract requires it) and *kénytelen* (has no choice but to) + infinitive. Both are adjectives and agree with the person: *köteles vagyok*, *kötelesek vagyunk*; in the 3rd person there is no *van*: *a főbérlő köteles*.
